t: Arminius was born into the Cherusci, was taken to Rome as a hostage, received a Roman education, joined the Roman cavalry and commanded auxiliaries, so he knew how the Romans fought and was trusted by Varus.

The Roman column was strung out over 15 to 20 kilometres of forest and then caught on a strip of ground only about 100 metres wide between a hill and a bog, in front of a wall the Germanic warriors had built.
After the defeat the legion numbers XVII, XVIII and XIX were not used again, and later Roman campaigns under Germanicus recovered two of the three lost eagles in 14 and 15 CE and the third in 41 CE.
dyk: Varus's army was paid on the morning of 7 September, and the large number of coins handed out became an archaeological marker: Tony Clunn's metal detector found coins of Augustus's reign at Kalkriese in 1987.
ev: Drusus defeats the Cherusci, and the boy Arminius is taken to Rome as a hostage
Varus takes command of the legions in Germania
Varus leaves winter quarters and sets up a summer camp, probably near Minden, in Cherusci lands
The army moves out for a campaign against the Angrivarii, and Arminius leaves it
The Germanic alliance attacks the army in the forest and at Kalkriese, and Varus kills himself
The fort of Aliso holds out for weeks before its garrison breaks through to the Rhine
Germanicus campaigns east of the Rhine and recovers two of the lost eagles
Arminius is poisoned by fellow Germans

f.place: Possibly near Kalkriese, north of Osnabrück in Lower Saxony, Germany; the site was long unidentified and the older theories placed it elsewhere
f.sides: The Roman Empire under the governor Publius Quinctilius Varus, with three legions (about 15,000 men) and nine small auxiliary units (about 4,500 men), though estimates of his army generally range from 20,000 to 30,000; an alliance of Germanic peoples under Arminius of the Cherusci, whose numbers are a guess: Murdoch suggests 25,000, Wells 17,000 to 100,000, Delbrück 20,000 to 30,000
f.outcome: The Roman army was ambushed and destroyed over several days and Varus killed himself. Rome lost its forts east of the Rhine, and the Rhine became the frontier.
